header.property: Example Booking Software GA4 property (properties/123456789), site and app in one property

measurement.check: Signup host is in the property
measurement.evidence: hostName in the last 30 days: www.example.com (40,800 sessions) and app.example.com (11,300 sessions).
sign_up fired 566 times for 560 users, with method set on every row (google, email, microsoft).
sign_up is one of 3 key events and fires.
Outbound clicks are on, and 1,338 clicks to app.example.com/signup were recorded from 6 pages in 30 days.

measurement_summary: Measured. The app host is in the property, sign_up fires with method and is a key event, and clicks into signup and form events are recorded, so steps 2 to 4 all ran.

path_into_signup.reading: The pricing page sends the highest share of its visitors to signup (13.5%). The online booking feature page has the second-most sessions (5,200) and the weakest click rate (1.2%), below even the blog post (1.5%), which readers open for an article.

email_route.note: Single sign-on signups skip the form, so the form's completion is read on the email route only: sign_up with method=email ÷ form_start.

funnel.method_reading: Email carries 51.8% of signups and Google 44.6%. No single sign-on method carries most signups, so the button order isn't a fix by the rule, but Google sits under a 5-field form, which is worth a test.

device.note: Mobile signs up at 63% of the desktop rate, under the 70% line. Tablet (20 page users) is too small to read.

verification.email_route_estimate: about 140 of 290 email signups confirmed, if every Google and Microsoft account counts as confirmed at signup (your answer); approximate
verification.note: email_verified doesn't carry method, so the split by route comes from your answer, not from GA4.

activation.label: approximate: two counts in one window, not a cohort

checks.evidence: Google and Microsoft single sign-on plus an email form. Google fits an audience of small business owners; Microsoft covers clinics on Microsoft 365.
5 visible fields: Full name, Business name, Email, Mobile number, Password. Business name and a mobile number are asked before the account exists.
Email is type="email" with autocomplete="email"; the password field has no autocomplete="new-password", so browsers won't offer a strong password.
Shown before typing: the placeholder reads "At least 8 characters".
The email form is visible on load: no click needed.
41 links on the page: the full site header and footer sit around the form.
The H1 says what the account is for (taking online bookings), and the line under it names the booking page, reminders and payments.
"Sign up". (The raw text also holds its hidden loading label, which is ignored.)
1 unlabelled input pushed off screen and out of the tab order (a honeypot); no CAPTCHA.
A "by signing up you agree" line with links, and no checkbox among the inputs.
dom_complete 2,650 ms, time_to_interactive 910 ms, 3 render-blocking scripts and 2 render-blocking stylesheets. One crawl from DataForSEO's servers, not a phone: a rough signal.

page_teardown.order_on_page: The two single sign-on buttons sit under the form, below an 'or' divider.
page_teardown.summary: 8 pass, 2 warn, 2 fail. The heading, sign-in options, password rule and bot protection are right. The form asks for 5 fields where 2 would do, and the full site navigation surrounds it.

top_fixes.fix: Ask only for email and password at signup; collect name, business name and mobile number after the account exists
top_fixes.step: Funnel: the email form, the biggest measured drop
top_fixes.visitors_touched: 610 people a month start the email form; 320 of them leave without an account
top_fixes.evidence: Step 3: 290 email signups from 610 form starts (47.5%). Step 4: 5 required fields, with business name and a mobile number before the account exists (fail). The business name can be asked on the first setup screen, where it names the booking page; the number when reminders are switched on. Mobile signs up at 63% of the desktop rate, and five fields cost most on a phone.

top_fixes.fix: Let people into the app before they confirm their email, with a 'confirm to publish your booking page' banner
top_fixes.visitors_touched: 150 signups a month who never confirmed and so never got in
top_fixes.evidence: Step 3: 410 of 560 signups confirmed (73.2%); by your answer, single sign-on accounts are confirmed at signup, so the loss sits on the email route. A booking page isn't money or health data, so a gate on publishing is enough.

top_fixes.fix: Put a clear signup button on the online booking feature page
top_fixes.evidence: Step 2: 62 signup clicks from 5,200 sessions (1.2%), against 6.5% on the home page. Check whether the button shows above the fold on a phone.

top_fixes.fix: Remove the site header and footer from the signup page
top_fixes.evidence: Distractions: fail. 41 links on the page, against 5 or fewer for a pass.

top_fixes.fix: Rename the button 'Create my booking page' and add autocomplete="new-password"
top_fixes.evidence: Submit button: warn ("Sign up"). Field setup: warn (no new-password on the password field).

tests_to_run.hypothesis: If we cut the email form to email and password, email signups per form start will rise from 47.5%, because 5 required fields, two of them about the business, stand between a start and an account.
tests_to_run.metric: sign_up (method=email) ÷ form_start, then booking_received ÷ sign_up to check that new accounts still reach a first booking

tests_to_run.hypothesis: If we move Continue with Google above the form, signups per signup page user will rise, because Google signups skip every field and already make up 44.6% of signups from under the form.
tests_to_run.metric: sign_up ÷ signup page users, and the method mix

tests_to_run.hypothesis: If we remove the site header and footer, mobile signups per signup page user will rise from 38.8%, because 41 links surround the form and mobile signs up at 63% of the desktop rate.
tests_to_run.metric: sign_up ÷ signup page users on mobile

unknowns: What happens after the form: the confirmation email (how fast it arrives, how long the link lasts), the first screen and onboarding. The skill never signs up to find out; check them once by hand.
What a phone shows above the fold, and lab mobile speed: the optional screenshot and PageSpeed Insights calls weren't run.
Weekly signup cohorts (active on day 1, activated by day 7, paying by day 30): GA4 gives two counts in one window, not a cohort.

fixes_this_skill_can_run.status: not needed: sign_up is already a key event
not needed: outbound clicks and form interactions are already on
not needed: method is built into GA4 and no other signup parameter was found
